name: Power to Lead
headline: Young people. Leading the change.
intro: Training that helps young people in care and care leavers choose what they share and make their point to adults.
glance: 6 hours in person, or 2 hours live online

problem.scene: Keisha, 15, tells the board about her worst move.
problem.question: The room claps. She goes home and can't sleep.
without: The same few voices carry the load
Young people share more than they meant to
Ideas get thanked, then nothing changes
with: Young people choose what they share
Everyone in the group has a role
They know who decides, and how to reach them
Each young person leaves with a plan
problem.standards: Councils have a duty to encourage children in care and care leavers to express their views. Doing that safely takes preparation.
problem.evidence: Nobody is asked to retell their story. Choosing what to share, and what to keep private, is the first thing the course covers.

groups: Children in care councils and care leaver forums
Youth ambassador, shadow board and participation groups

notes: A worker they know is welcome

outcomes: Describe three of their own strengths, with an example of each from their own life.
Decide which parts of their story they will share, with whom and when, and turn down a question.
Check a meeting can change things
Use Laura Lundy's model of participation to check whether a meeting they go to can actually change anything.
Explain who makes decisions in their council and what the corporate parenting principles say.
Make a two-minute point to a group of adults and answer one challenging question.
Write a plan with a SMART goal, the first three steps and the adult who will back it.

pillars.title: Lundy's model of participation
pillars.stance_line: Most groups get the first two. Power to Lead helps young people get all four.
items: Somewhere safe to speak, with time to prepare.
Support to give their view, in their own words.
Adults in the room who can act on what they hear.
Their views change what happens next, and they hear how.
pillars.base: Laura Lundy's model of participation (2007), with Roger Hart's ladder of participation and the corporate parenting principles.

story_line: Four stories run through the day: Keisha, 15, Connor, 16, Imani, 19, and Finn, 14. Each is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on youth participation, including Home and Future, the South East Regional Care Cooperative, where Power to Lead began as five sessions with Youth Ambassadors from across the region.
He founded the Care Leavers National Movement and led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
